sections.heading: What are people asking us at 9pm with a warm house
sections.text: Before you start What are people asking us at 9pm with a warm house Why is my AC running but not cooling? It is moving air but not moving heat. That happens when airflow is choked, when the fan is set to ON so it blows between cycles, when the outdoor unit has lost power, or when the refrigerant circuit cannot do its job. The first 3 you can check yourself in 10 minutes, and we will walk you through them. Should I turn my AC off while it is blowing warm? If there is ice on the lines, yes. Shut cooling off and leave the fan running. Running a frozen system can flood the compressor and turn a few-hundred-dollar repair into a few-thousand-dollar one. No ice and nothing smelling wrong, running it while you arrange a visit is usually fine. Can I change my AC capacitor myself? No. A run capacitor holds a charge after the power is off, and discharging one safely takes the right tool and the knowledge to use it. The part is cheap, which is exactly why this gets recommended online and why people get hurt. Identify the symptom, then hand it to somebody licensed. How much should a repair on my AC cost? Repair cost depends on the actual failure, equipment, market, access and the diagnostic work required. As verified quote and outcome records mature, the Repair Record is designed to publish comparable ranges with geography and sample size attached. Is five companies about to call me? No. Your request is never sold as a lead. If you choose to involve a provider it goes to one at a time, and nobody sees your details until you send them.

direct_answer.text: Check 4 things: thermostat mode and fan setting , the filter , whether the outdoor unit is running, and ice on the copper line . Ice means switch cooling off and leave the fan on first. If those look normal, it is something you cannot confirm by eye: an outdoor electrical or start issue , a coil or airflow problem , or refrigerant . Those need measurements at the equipment.

visual_assets.title: How to tell an iced refrigerant line from a normal one, and what to do about each
visual_assets.description: Two side by side views of the copper refrigerant lines where they enter the house. On the left, the larger insulated suction line is coated in white frost and ice, with droplets forming below it, and the label says to switch cooling off at the thermostat while leaving the fan running so the coil can thaw. On the right, the same line is clean and dry with intact black foam insulation, and the label says cooling may keep running while a visit is arranged. Both views show the smaller uninsulated liquid line beneath, which stays clear in each case.
visual_assets.caption: Ice or clear. The one observation that changes what you should do right now.
